messages:
sam: Quick sanity check — for the policy runtime refactor, are we okay to remove the legacy tenant-weight field from the route resolver? Thinking about surface stability for Dedicated customers and existing SDK integrations.

katie: Not without a migration plan. Breaking that field will surface in customer configs. My vote: compat shim + admin preview + opt-in flip window.

aj: Shims are acceptable short-term. Main concern is perf and complexity — don't do per-request translation. Materialize conversion at config load and serve normalized penalties.

maria: Agreed. Also we need an admin preview endpoint so SRE/support can show tenants their converted routing before flipping.

sam: From perf bench (earlier PR) conversion is cheap (~200us/config) but hot-reload churn could amplify cost. Cache invalidation semantics need clarity.

policy-bot: Note: policy-hot-reload triggered at 3301234700 by @sam (deploy-id: pr-4621).

katie: For hot-reload safety, use versioned snapshots + a validation phase. We must avoid half-applied states where some requests see old policy and some see new but with mismatched invariants.

aj: API surface suggestion: keep resolver input as an explicit RouteContext { tenant_id, model, region, latency_budget_ms, cost_preference } — avoid passing internal runtime objects. That lets us keep compat translators isolated.

maria: Also propose a per-tenant "compat_mode" flag that delays the flip for specific tenants for up to 3 months. Default: on (to preserve behavior).

sam: Proposed rollout plan: 1) implement config-load shim that converts legacy weights -> normalized penalties and materializes a snapshot, 2) admin preview API + UI, 3) deploy to staging and run canary for one week, 4) 2-week telemetry window observing route selection/rate/latency, 5) start tenant opt-out/opt-in campaign and flip globally after no regressions.

aj: I'll own runtime impl (conversion + snapshot store + hot-reload hook). Need telemetry to define success metrics and alert thresholds.

telemetry: We'll add the following metrics: route_selection.count{route_id,tenant}, route_latency.p50/p95 per-route, route_error_rate.delta (post-flip vs baseline), and a route_fallback.signal when a route is used due to capacity fallback > 0.5%. We'll also record a conversion_impact.histogram for per-tenant median latency change.

maria: Edge case: tenants relying on soft affinity (preference for warm affinity shards) — conversion must preserve relative affinity ordering. Add preserve_affinity boolean in conversion with default true.

katie: Can we make this migration runtime-only (no DB schema changes)? Prefer not to force a DB migration during rollout.

aj: Yes — runtime-only. We'll store snapshot metadata in the config store (existing blob) with a converted_from tag; no schema changes.

sam: Pseudo-code sketch for conversion (will put in PR):
```
for route in legacy_weights:
  penalty = map_weight_to_penalty(route.weight) // monotonic map: higher weight => lower penalty
routes = normalize_penalties(routes) // ensure numeric stability for softmax/ordering
store_snapshot(routes, meta={"converted_from":"legacy_weights_v1", "preserve_affinity":true})
```

katie: Who will build the admin UI preview? devex-team owns developer-facing UI. pinging @devex-team.

devex-team: We can do a lightweight preview page showing side-by-side routing table and a simulated 'requests by region' heatmap. Need an API that returns both legacy and converted views.

aj: I'll add the preview API endpoint: GET /admin/policy/preview?tenant=... returning the two views and diff.

maria: Timeline check — is next Tuesday too aggressive for the initial canary? :thumbsup:

sam: Sounds fine. I'll open the RFC follow-up PR with code sketch, tests, and rollout checklist today.

katie: Thanks — also add an ops rollback plan: automatic rollback if route_error_rate.delta > 1% for > 10 minutes.

aj: acknowledged, will include in PR.

maria: Great. small follow-up: ensure logs include the snapshot id used for routing decisions to help postmortem traces.

sam: Good call. We'll add snapshot_id to request traces at the decider boundary.

katie: Ok that's a clear path. We'll iterate after telemetry results. :white_check_mark:
